cases.title: S3 Tables fixture sim_a with AutoCreate false: the six filtered reads arrive exactly once as typed Iceberg rows, flushed by the Interval timer
cases.intent: The basic S3 Tables contract against the real service, on the stack's fixture table sim_a. The fixture is shared by every mode and build, so rows are told apart by label = the run marker (@.metadata.marker). With AutoCreate false the writer only lists and loads the existing table (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:259-292), converts each mapping's JMESPath value to the column's Iceberg type (AwsS3TablesTypesHelper.kt:22-39), buffers the rows and lets the 1 s Interval timer flush them as a Parquet data file plus one append commit (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:375-379, :669-695). Band ValueFilters (an 'and' of ge and lt, AndFilter.kt:15-17) pass ctr and half only on reads 75..80, so exactly six rows can ever carry the marker; every other read lacks the required columns and is skipped silently because WarnIfValueMissing is false (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:474-481). The 75 lead-in reads (15 s at 200 ms) keep the window clear of IPC start-up: sfc-main drops a record for an IPC target whose InitializeTarget has not returned yet (ScheduleWriter.kt:243-249, IpcTargetWriter.kt:404-405), and a failed attempt is retried only after WAIT_AFTER_ERROR = 10 s (IpcTargetWriter.kt:94-97, :460), so a window on reads 0..5 can lose its first rows and RecordsWritten then never reaches 6. The S3 Tables setup itself drops nothing: the service answers InitializeTarget as soon as the writer exists (IpcTargetServer.kt:287-302) and the setup runs inside the writer while records queue (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:358-369). In-process and uberjar writers are always initialized (TargetWriter.kt:23-24), so there the lead-in only costs 15 s. The first wait is the line logged after the setup's last catalog call (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:282-286), so a timeout tells a stalled setup from a stalled write. The case fails if a row is lost or committed twice (exactly 6 rows, counter exactly 75..80, RecordsWritten exactly 6), if a column has the wrong value or type (strict int, double and bool; UTC ISO timestamps, one per read), if the marker misses the label column (no row is found), if SFC tries to create anything, or on any WriteError.

cases.title: S3 Tables, one target into two fixture tables: sim_a and the day-partitioned sim_b with two Mappings, flushed once by a BufferCount summed over both tables; Messages is always 0 (known defect)
cases.intent: One target writes the unpartitioned sim_a and sim_b, which the stack partitions by day(event_time), so sim_b takes the partitioned path (PartitionKey per record, AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:632-640, :739-753). sim_b has two Mappings, so every read yields two sim_b rows (:423-487): one from ctr/half with ok true, one from hi/k with ok false. BufferCount counts the rows of all tables (:404-410): band ValueFilters pass ctr, half and hi only on reads 75..80, whose 6 + 12 = 18 rows trigger exactly one flush - one commit for sim_a, one per day partition for sim_b - and the 120 s Interval cannot fire within the case; every other read lacks ctr/hi and is skipped with the Missing-required-value warning (:474-481). The 75 lead-in reads keep the window clear of the IPC start-up drop (ScheduleWriter.kt:243-249, see AWS-S3T-01): one lost row would leave 17 rows buffered and the flush would never come. The partition spec is checked as SFC logs it (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:288-290): Iceberg renders it as '[\n  1000: event_time_day: day(1)\n]', and SFC's logger removes the whitespace inside every [...] that holds no nested brackets (Logger.kt:141, :695-713), so the line ends in '[1000:event_time_day:day(1)]'. The case fails if a table or a mapping is dropped or duplicated, if one mapping's rows carry the other's values, if the flush is split or not count-triggered across tables, or if the partitioned write fails.

cases.title: S3 Tables AutoCreate in the fixture bucket: a per-run namespace and two tables with their own schema and partition spec; the last-parsed partition transform overwrites the first table's (known defect)
cases.intent: AutoCreate below an existing table bucket: the namespace sfc_it_<marker> does not exist, so the writer creates it (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:316-334), then each missing table with its configured schema and partition spec through the Iceberg REST catalog (:268-275, AwsS3TablesHelper.kt:214-223), loads it back and validates the configured schema against it (:281-314). The marker makes the namespace unique per mode and build; the sink deletes it afterwards, and the janitor sweeps sfc_it_b_<run>* in the fixture bucket (janitor.py:78-85). The schema SFC logs for each table is the catalog's, so it shows what was created (long, float, optional). The two tables partition with the same transform on different columns - events truncate[10](counter), flags truncate[3](label) - which is what exposes the shared enum state the known defect pins. Fails if the namespace or a table is not created, a column is created with another type or nullability, or the rows of either table do not arrive exactly once.

cases.title: S3 Tables AutoCreate from the table bucket up (uberjar only): bucket, namespace and an identity(label) table; with PartitionOptimization false the rows are filed under the first record's partition, so a pruned query misses them (known defect)
cases.intent: The whole AutoCreate chain, starting with the table bucket (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:336-356): the per-run bucket sfc-it-b-<run>-s3t04-uj matches the project role's bucket/sfc-it-b-* grants and the janitor's sweep, and the sink deletes it with its namespace and table afterwards. uberjar only: an account has about 10 table buckets per region, so one bucket per build is the budget. The table is partitioned by identity(label) with PartitionOptimization false; two mappings give every read one row with a decoy label <marker>_x (first in the buffer) and one with label = marker, and tag carries the marker in both, so the main sink (filter on tag) sees all 12 rows of the single BufferCount flush; the bylabel sink filters on label, the partition column, which is where the known defect shows. Fails if the bucket, namespace or table is not created, if a row is lost or duplicated, or if either mapping's rows are missing.

cases.title: S3 Tables with AutoCreate false and one missing table: the whole target never initialises, every record is rejected and nothing is written; the error names "tableName" instead of the table (known defect)
cases.intent: With AutoCreate false a missing table is a permanent configuration error. Setup lists the bucket's tables, finds and loads sim_a, then throws for the missing sfc_e2e_absent (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:259-279); the writer only logs the setup error and stays uninitialised (:363-369). From then on every record is rejected with 'is not loaded' (:496-497) and every Interval flush logs 'not initialized' and discards the buffers (:611-613, :666) - so even the healthy sim_a, loaded before the failure, gets no row. Fails if SFC creates the table despite AutoCreate false, writes or meters any write, or stops rejecting records with the table's name. The missing table never exists, so there is nothing to read back for it; sim_a is read back instead.

cases.title: S3 Tables refuses a configured Schema that does not match the existing table and names each column; every record is then dropped without a WriteError (known defect)
cases.intent: Before writing, the writer compares every configured column with the loaded table (AwsS3TablesTargetWriter.kt:298-314). The fixture's counter is int and it has no column extra, so the target must refuse to start with one message naming both problems, instead of failing every Parquet write later with an unhelpful error. Every record is then rejected ('is not loaded', :496-497), nothing is metered as a write and nothing with this run's marker reaches sim_a. Fails if the mismatch goes undetected (rows, a write or a write error would appear), if the message does not name the column and both types, or if any row lands in the fixture.
